source.title: Exploring Quaternion Neural Network Loss Surfaces

record.tranche_reason: The study measures projected loss-surface curvature and reports held-out performance for tuned quaternion and real-valued MLPs. This is a different geometric measure and comparison from the claim versions, and it does not measure the training–test gap directly.
record.gate_note: The study's findings are about quaternion versus real-valued fully connected networks on breast-cancer classification and Lorenz time-series prediction. It does not test the listed versions' specific conditions or measures; the results are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: The study compares quaternion and real-valued MLPs on breast-cancer classification and Lorenz prediction. None of its results tests V1–V8. Its projected-surface curvature is not V7's magnitude-aware training-loss perturbation tolerance, and held-out performance is not the training–test gap. It cites large-batch findings but performs no batch-size comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that the tuned QNNs have smoother projected loss surfaces, potentially explaining their optimization and performance advantages. Classification significance uses α = 0.1. They acknowledge that the enormous regression performance difference may bias the loss-surface comparison in favor of QNNs.
record.recipe_differences: Uses tuned quaternion and real-valued fully connected networks, two task datasets, projected loss surfaces, surface-variation curvature estimates, and 30 projection replications. It does not reproduce the original studies' methods or test the listed claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Task changes the reported curvature comparison: breast-cancer classification paired t-test p-value 0.0874; Lorenz prediction p-value < 1 × 10−43.

fits_no_version.finding: QNNs have lower mean projected-surface curvature in both tasks and better held-out performance: classification AUROC 0.975 versus 0.969, and prediction MSE 1.63 × 10−13 versus 33.757. Curvature comparisons give p = 0.0874 for classification and p < 10−43 for prediction.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In these two tuned quaternion-versus-real MLP comparisons, lower projected-loss curvature accompanies better held-out performance; this does not establish a relationship between magnitude-aware sharpness and generalization gaps.

record.code_released: Data and code files for this research are available upon request.
record.problems: The study uses only two tasks and fixed two-hidden-layer fully connected architectures. It examines fully tuned and trained models; the authors state that the very large regression performance difference may bias the resulting loss and surface plots. The measured quantity is projected-surface curvature, not the training–test gap.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and the comparison of natural-label versus random-label held-out accuracy.
Test error across widths beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under comparable tuning. Optimizer selection during tuning supplies no reported optimizer comparison.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects and interactions with dataset size, augmentation, or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware training-loss perturbation tolerance, its association with training–test gaps among similarly fitted convolutional networks, and ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The 30 replications sample projection directions around tuned models, rather than independent training runs. All reported row values match the supplied text; cannot_determine refers to their inability to establish a listed claim version.

versions.untested_parts: Does not train networks on random labels or compare their random-label and natural-label generalization.
No width sweep beyond interpolation or test-error curve across network widths.
Compares quaternion and real-valued fully connected networks; no convolutional networks or learned local connectivity.
No adaptive-optimizer versus SGD generalization comparison; the tuned models use SGD.
Measures projected surface curvature, not magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance; does not compare the measure's ranking against norm- and margin-based measures or directly measure train–test gaps.
Does not remove or retrain on memorized examples.
